correctness.rationale: Solving the stated implicit quadratic-potential update gives z_{k+1}=R_θ(z_k+σe₂ΔW_k), θ=2 arctan(ωh/2). Orthogonal rotation makes E||z||² increase by σ²h, proving the trace law. Independent noise increments yield C_N=σ²h Σ_{j=1}^N R_{jθ}e₂e₂ᵀR_{jθ}ᵀ, whose traceless complex sum S=Σ e^{2ijθ}=e^{i(N+1)θ} sin(Nθ)/sinθ gives the claimed spectrum and all isotropizing h via θ=mπ/N (N≥2). At fixed T=Nh, θ/h=ω−ω³h²/12+O(h⁴), and the right-endpoint Euler–Maclaurin formula produces first-order tensor σ²[fω(T)−fω(0)]/2. It vanishes exactly at ωT∈πZ; then frequency drift gives σ²ω²T diag(1,−1)/24 at order h², with numerical mean error also O(h²). Fixed N, h→∞ sends θ→π and normalized covariance to rank-one projector, whereas exact normalized →I/2. Independent covariance recursions matched the spectral tensor in 20 parameter cases; 8 fixed-time asymptotic cases corroborated, not proved, infinite-family claims.

value.rationale: A positive-semidefinite moment method can exhibit perfectly isotropic noise at isolated phase steps despite not matching exact covariance, and its leading error unexpectedly drops from first to second order at a physically motivated set of times. Exact constants and large-step anisotropy expose practical diagnostics for moment observables without claiming all-observable weak order two.
